nodes.title: Joining the Master's in Water Security and Global Change
nodes.text: The first cohort of a joint Master's across five institutions. My Bachelor's in Mechanical Engineering and my years as a data scientist and developer join the trail here.

nodes.title: Contaminant Transport Modelling
nodes.text: Mathematical modelling of flow and transport equations. Plenty of new civil engineering, like open-channel flow, and a lot of overlap with the mathematical modelling and CFD courses from my Bachelor's. I really enjoyed the lectures.

nodes.title: Physico-chemical Processes for Water and Wastewater Treatment
nodes.text: Designing treatment structures, and the scientific methods to assess water quality. I loved coding out the iterative problems. Term project: wastewater treatment and resource recovery in the distillery industry.

nodes.title: Sustainability in River Basin Management
nodes.text: A holistic view of sustainable development centred on water: planetary boundaries, the three pillars of sustainability, and many case studies and stories. My favourite course in the whole programme. Term project: integrated water resources management in the Cooum River basin, with stakeholder interviews.

nodes.title: Groundwater Engineering
nodes.text: The fundamentals of how water travels beneath the Earth's surface, and a lot of new hydrogeology. Modelling, simulation and programming made the physics easy to visualise.

nodes.title: Climate Adaptation in Coastal and Hydraulic Engineering
nodes.text: The fundamentals of coastal engineering and climate adaptation. I especially liked grey versus green solutions, the range of adaptation strategies, and the photographs of case studies from the professor's own field visits.

nodes.title: Hydrologic Data Analysis and Modeling
nodes.text: I took this to connect my machine learning and data analytics to hydrology. Term project: a spatio-temporal assessment of climate migration in India using proxy-based methods.

nodes.title: Technology and Sustainable Development
nodes.text: A unique perspective on how technology is perceived. The lectures and notes are still very valuable to me.

nodes.title: Water Resources Planning and Management
nodes.text: The operations research and optimisation I enjoyed in my Bachelor's, now applied to water management. Term project: GIS-based water management and basin analysis.

nodes.title: Water, Sanitation and Hygiene
nodes.text: Systems thinking for real-world problems. Case studies and field visits showed me how WASH is perceived in rural settings, and why decentralised solutions matter. My eye-opener: sustainable development is 80% a social problem and 20% a technology problem. Term project: a water security assessment with the WATSAT tool, and water-related risk under a changing climate, in a village on the outskirts of Chennai, with stakeholder interviews.

nodes.title: Waste as a resource, for Chennai
nodes.text: A business model I'm keen to implement in Chennai. I see waste as a resource with great potential, built on the resource-circularity ideas I explored further through the Resource Nexus at UNU. The pitch: blockchain for waste accounting, a rebirth store for upcycled waste, and computer vision to segregate the legacy waste in our landfills.

nodes.title: Urban Water Management
nodes.text: How design and urban factors shape water management, with practical implementations. Very interesting lectures.

nodes.title: Water Extremes: Risk Management and Adaptation
nodes.text: A core subject that shaped my thesis. This is where I learned the concepts of disaster risk and resilience.

nodes.title: International Water Issues
nodes.text: Every lecture was a case study by a researcher: today's water issues in a changing climate, the methods used to assess them, and how complex they really are. Term project: the Namami Gange programme's policies against river pollution. My part: defining the KPIs and success metrics for policy implementation.

nodes.title: Flood Protection
nodes.text: Another core subject for my thesis: flood damage assessment, protection measures and their types, and the parameters behind them, with case studies.

nodes.title: Hydrodynamic Simulations
nodes.text: An introduction to smoothed particle hydrodynamics and Lagrangian, GPU-based simulation. Term project: modelling and simulating a scenario.

nodes.date: Interreg MOSAIC Summer School · Nevegal, Italy
nodes.title: Forests that protect
nodes.text: A week on how alpine forests protect against avalanches and rockfall, alongside the grey measures in place, and what Storm Vaia and climate change did to the Dolomites. New forestry concepts that enriched my understanding of disaster risk reduction.

nodes.date: Research Module · DAAD Global Climate and Environment Centre
nodes.title: Biodiversity under Climate Change
nodes.text: General and transboundary issues in the Jordan River region. I studied and presented on ecological responses to climate change.

nodes.title: The Resource Nexus
nodes.text: An introduction to the resource nexus, with a focus on standards, e-learning, scientific communication and the UN ecosystem. The many case studies from ongoing research were enriching. Deliverable: drafting an e-learning module on food security and farming practices in East Africa.
